items.text: the dice in Autoplay's Every row is a switch: tap it again to stop random, and the time it last drew stays
Scrub is open to try, in Pro beta: a pad over the bar holds every scene in play as a slice of its picture; drag across it and the field follows your finger
the ways are named Random, Shuffle (every scene once, like a deck of cards) and Seed
Seed grows its order from a few words you can type or roll again; the same words always play the same order
Autoplay's unit shows how it runs: a stopwatch whose hand goes round once per scene, beats that light in turn, a bar that pulses; a hand when the robot is stopped, with the row beside it dimmed
the robot's ears: a scene slips into one ear and out of the other at each change, the way it is going

Autoplay's Order is now Which way: Forward, Back, Surprise, and with Pro Bounce, Deck (every scene once, shuffled, then a new deck) and Same surprise (a numbered shuffle that always plays the same order)
Loop or Stop at end: the robot can stop after the last scene
Built-in, Yours and Starred moved to Which scenes, with how many scenes each holds
the robot's face acts out the way it goes: left to right, right to left, there and back, or dealing like cards
volume at zero is silent, from the ring as from the bar
the bar's speaker and the rings' volume show the same state: lit only when you can hear it; muted or at zero it goes dark with the X while its wave still moves
the ring button in a panel's band lights while its ring is open beside the panel, and a second tap closes it
a row of chips that runs past the panel's edge fades on that side, so you can see there is more
Autoplay's stopwatch ring is grey while the robot is stopped
Autoplay's unit shows as three small dots under its circle, the lit one is the unit, and one line runs through the middle of the circles
a panel's close keeps its highlight inside the panel's rounded corner
every panel has the ring between its ‹ and › at the bottom: on a phone the panel folds into its ring, on a bigger screen the ring opens beside the panel
opening a dot's ring, a lit dot (the camera, when it is on) no longer swells into a big blue ball: it turns into the ring's dark middle as it grows
the ground button's icon shows which it is: overlay lights its middle dot, under shows it half seen, ignore an empty frame
going back from a dot's ring, no dot flashes lit while the dots fly out; a lit dot takes its color once it lands
